input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an MFN running against us: we must extend to Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms given to any other technology supplier. It is open-ended — no defined product, no duration limit, and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. It also directly conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. The shortest cure at the preferred level is to negate the obligation in Section 7.2, leaving Section 12.3 consistent; any Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would remain acceptable.

ops.oldText: Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
ops.newText: Customer has no obligation to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the obligation for us to give Vendor terms no less favourable than our best terms with any other technology supplier; our playbook does not accept an MFN running against us, and Section 12.3 already confirms we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.
proposal.summary: Negate the Customer-side MFN obligation in Section 7.2.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
